title: Portlight Ship Canon Entry
description: Schema for a named sailing vessel. Adapted from the Star Freight ship schema, which carried silhouette_cue + hull_repair_history + material_dominant as the heaviest trainable leverage. TWO ADDITIONS, both earned by a failed 2026-07-25 generation run that produced eight structurally inconsistent variants of one galleon: (1) `visual.rig_plan` enumerates masts and sails BY NAME, so a prompt can refer to 'the foremast' instead of 'one mast' and the model has a structural inventory to be consistent with. (2) `damage_ladder` states which NAMED masts are broken and which NAMED sails are lost at each state, and requires the loss sets to be monotonically non-decreasing. In the failed run a mast snapped at state 04 and was intact again at 05, because nothing in the pipeline held a model of the ship's parts. Both fields are freeze-watched.

id.description: Also the hull_id used by the portlight-ships pipeline and by every subject_id: <hull>__<state>__<rig>.

era.description: e.g. '1600s'. Keeps period drift out of the silhouette.

silhouette_cue.description: The read-at-a-glance shape. What makes this hull recognisable at sprite size.

palette.description: Required and pinned. An unpinned palette let the master's sails drift from the rest of the ladder.

rig_plan.description: The structural inventory. THIS IS THE FIX for part-level drift: masts and sails are NAMED, so prompts and damage states refer to specific objects rather than counts the model is free to reinvent.

sections.description: Lower / top / topgallant. A snapped mast breaks at a section join — naming them makes 'snapped partway up' unambiguous.

mast.description: id of the mast it is bent to, or 'bowsprit'.

rig_states.description: Orthogonal to damage. Star Freight had no sails, so this axis is new. 'sails-closed' means canvas FURLED — rolled and lashed along the yard, still present. It does NOT mean absent; a ship with no canvas is a stripped derelict.

damage_ladder.description: The ordered states. masts_broken and sails_lost MUST be monotonically non-decreasing down the array — anything broken at state N stays broken at N+1. Validate this on canon build; the 2026-07-25 run shipped a mast that un-broke between states.

condition.description: What a viewer SEES. Describe the result, never the manoeuvre.

masts_broken.description: mast ids from rig_plan.masts. Empty = all standing.

sails_lost.description: sail ids from rig_plan.sails that are destroyed and gone at this state.

rig_states.description: Which rig variants this state produces. A state whose canvas is destroyed cannot furl, so it offers sails-open only — that is WHY 04 has no closed variant, recorded rather than assumed.

forbidden_inputs.description: Negative constraints as CANON, written once, not rediscovered per prompt. Every entry here should trace to an observed failure.

signature_features.description: The identity anchors that must survive every damage state and every heading.
